Changelog

Mirrored from services/compd/CHANGELOG.md, where releases update it. The component's page is compd. This page describes the current main branch of MixOS.

Unreleased — 2026-10-27

  • Use the shared design title band layout for all four groups and centre MixOS titles by default. Host registered apps' revisioned Action Bars through the existing scene-host registry and Bus client, with shared Lucide rasters, hover and toggle states, disabled colours and the existing tooltip cards. comp.window.action dispatches enabled registry commands; comp.props reports hosting and per-surface item counts.
  • Add --debug[=LEVEL], comp.debug and comp.debug.set for live tracing levels from off through trace, with a warn baseline and per-binary journal identity. Record mapping, placement, grabs and initial placement configures at debug; keep configure streams and motion detail at trace. The separate developer logger is unchanged.

0.2.0

  • Add comp.window.place_as, comp.window.tile_key and comp.tiles.get. Super+arrow uses the same tiling transition as agents, including mirrored slots across adjacent outputs. Super+PageUp toggles maximise, Super+PageDown minimises, and Super+Backspace restores and focuses. Window props expose placement and saved floating geometry; placement changes publish one sequenced comp.window.placement.changed event. Restore leaves fullscreen first, otherwise restores floating geometry.

  • comp.window.wait accepts match.pid alongside the app ID and title filters, so a mapping wait cannot resolve to another instance of an app.

  • comp.window.maximize accepts optional output (key or native name), including retargeting an already maximised window. Normal restore geometry survives, and focus and workspace stay unchanged. Unknown outputs refuse before effects. Toolkit uses this to restore saved maximised frames.

  • The user keys belong to the user. compd enforces the rule itself, ahead of its own bindings, because on a MixOS VT it reads the keyboard itself. The user keys are bare F1–F12 and Right Ctrl, Right Alt or Right Shift with an arrow, matched side-exact with inputd's classifier and press-latched disposition. A user key fires the session user's binding, or goes to the focused client when the user bound it passthrough; otherwise it is swallowed, and no client sees its press, repeat or release. Under a session lock every user key is swallowed and nothing fires.

    • The bindings are read from keymap.v1 (inputd/keymap.json in the user's MixOS config dir, or $MIXOS_USER_KEYMAP) and reloaded when the file changes. A bad file keeps the last good keymap, and a missing one binds nothing.
    • A comp.* command runs as its Bus request does. Any other command is sent to its service fire-and-forget, with the row's args as the body. repeat: allow rows repeat at the seat's rate while held.
    • bindings.user lists the rows.
    • compd ships no user-key binding. The opt-in bare-F9 Bus key can no longer fire.

  • comp.region.select 0.2.0: a click (under 4 logical px of travel, with no drag on the way) and Enter or keypad Enter now select the whole output under the pointer, answering exactly as a drag from corner to corner does; a click used to re-arm the selection. A drag stays a drag even if it returns to its start. The overlay dims the output (clear inside a drag), outlines the selection in the theme's focus-ring colour and shows a hint ("Drag to select an area · Click or Enter for the whole screen · Esc to cancel"), only on the selected output, in the session look (followed on every change); a selected reply waits for a frame of that output without the overlay.

  • While a comp.region.select run holds the seat the cursor is a crosshair (the theme's crosshair, else cross or tcross, else the arrow); the normal cursor is back on the frame that ends the run, however it ends, so the clean frame never shows the crosshair. A cursor's hotspot is now read after its shape is chosen, so a change of shape lands in place on its first frame.

  • The capture panels (the setup chooser, region border and dim, Stop buttons and the Continue, Save, Encoding and error dialogs) draw in the session theme, followed on every change like the region overlay, with the embedded theme until the shell delivers one. Open panels repaint at once.

  • Workspaces: comp.workspaces.list, comp.workspaces.set_count {count, persist} and comp.workspace.rename {index, name, persist}, and the comp.workspace.changed topic. The count and names persist in preferences.json (workspaces_count, workspace_names) and compd starts with them. workspaces.list rows carry name.

  • The pointer moves at the same logical speed at every output scale: a relative delta is multiplied by the output scale as well as cursor_sensitivity, so a scale-2.5 output no longer needs a sensitivity of 2.5.

  • compd's own UI is egui: capture overlays and dialogs, the frame-rate overlay, notifications and the Mix Scenes shell are egui programs painted with egui-wgpu into textures on compd's own EGL context, on the same MixOS look the apps draw with (toolkit).

  • Mix Scenes are laid out as flexbox with taffy, as Quoin lays them out; shell.scene.layout reports the rectangles each node was drawn and hit-tested at.

  • The session look follows settingsd through the shared consumer on the scene host's own connection (compact schema-2 deliveries, offline cache), and window decorations take their themes from the same look.

  • A UI surface off screen is suspended: its animations stop waking the compositor until it is shown again.

  • The whole comp.* command catalogue is registered, and a registry test keeps it exact.

  • Window titles are shaped with cosmic-text over the apps' embedded faces, so they match the apps' type and need no fonts installed.
